descriptors.definition: The board of directors collectively manages corporate affairs, exercising powers delegated by shareholders to achieve wealth maximization while protecting stakeholder interests. Companies must hold their first board meeting within thirty days of incorporation and conduct a minimum of four meetings annually with a maximum interval of one hundred and twenty days between consecutive sessions.
inclusion: Collective management of corporate affairs by directors
Scheduling first board meeting within thirty days of incorporation
Maintaining a minimum of four board meetings per calendar year
Ensuring maximum gap of one hundred and twenty days between consecutive meetings
exclusion: Matters legally required to be exercised by shareholders in general meetings
Exemptions applicable to specific company categories under Section 173(5)
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from shareholder general meetings which exercise reserve powers rather than day-to-day administrative management.

descriptors.concept_name: Exemptions to Certain Companies Regarding Board Meetings
descriptors.definition: One Person Companies, small companies, and dormant companies are exempt from holding four annual board meetings, requiring instead one meeting in each half of a calendar year with a minimum ninety-day gap. Furthermore, a One Person Company having only a single director on its board is completely exempt from holding any board meetings.
inclusion: One Person Companies with multiple directors holding half-yearly board meetings
Small companies conducting one board meeting in each half of a calendar year
Dormant companies maintaining a minimum ninety-day gap between half-yearly meetings
exclusion: Standard companies governed by regular four-meeting annual schedules
One Person Companies having only a single director which are totally exempted from holding board meetings
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general companies requiring four annual meetings under Section 173(1) by relaxing frequency rules for specified corporate entities.

descriptors.definition: A valid board meeting requires a quorum consisting of one-third of the total board strength or two directors, whichever is higher, with fractions rounded off as one. Directors participating through video conferencing or audio-visual means count towards the quorum unless excluded for specific items under the law.
inclusion: Calculating quorum as one-third of total strength or two directors whichever is higher
Counting electronic participation via video conferencing towards quorum
Modifying quorum rules for compliant Section 8 companies as eight members or 25 percent whichever is less
exclusion: Vacant director places when computing total board strength
Articles of association specifying a quorum lower than the statutory minimum
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general meeting quorums which apply to shareholder assemblies rather than board deliberations.

descriptors.definition: Companies may pass board resolutions by circulating drafts and necessary papers via electronic means to directors when urgent decisions do not necessitate a formal meeting. If at least one-third of total directors demand that a circulated resolution be decided at a meeting, the chairperson must put it before a convened board meeting.
instrument_references: Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules, 2014, Rule 5
inclusion: Circulating draft resolutions and papers via email or fax
Noting resolutions passed by circulation in the subsequent board meeting minutes
Reverting to a physical meeting when requested by one-third of total directors
exclusion: Matters mandatorily requiring consideration at a duly convened physical board meeting
Resolutions lacking the requisite director consent
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from physical board meeting resolutions because it operates through document circulation without assembling directors in person.

descriptors.definition: Listed public companies and specific public companies meeting prescribed paid-up share capital, turnover, or loan thresholds must constitute an audit committee. Unlisted joint ventures, wholly owned subsidiaries, and dormant companies are exempt from this requirement.
instrument_references: Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules, 2014, Rule 6
Companies (Appointment and Qualifications of Directors) Rules, 2014, Rule 4
inclusion: Constitution by every listed public company
Public companies with paid-up capital of ten crore rupees or more
Public companies with turnover of one hundred crore rupees or more
Public companies with aggregate loans, debentures, and deposits exceeding fifty crore rupees
exclusion: Unlisted joint ventures
Wholly owned subsidiaries
Dormant companies under Section 455
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from other board committees like the nomination and remuneration committee by its specific financial and audit-focused statutory criteria.

descriptors.definition: Listed public companies and specified large public companies defined by financial thresholds must establish a nomination and remuneration committee. Joint ventures, wholly owned subsidiaries, and dormant companies are exempt from forming this committee.
instrument_references: Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules, 2014, Rule 6
Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules, 2014, Rule 4
inclusion: Every listed public company
Public companies with paid-up share capital of ten crore rupees or more
Public companies with turnover of one hundred crore rupees or more
Public companies with aggregate outstanding loans, debentures, and deposits exceeding fifty crore rupees
exclusion: Joint ventures
Wholly owned subsidiaries
Dormant companies under Section 455
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from the audit committee through its exclusive mandate regarding director appointments and remuneration policies rather than financial auditing.

descriptors.concept_name: Powers of the Board of Directors
descriptors.definition: The board of directors is entitled to exercise all powers and do all acts that the company is authorized to do, subject to statutory provisions, memorandum, articles, and general meeting regulations. Specific statutory powers must be exercised exclusively through resolutions passed at duly convened board meetings.
instrument_references: Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules, 2014, Rule 8
inclusion: Exercising all powers authorized for the company management
Complying with memorandum, articles, and general meeting directions
Executing mandatory corporate powers via resolutions passed at board meetings
exclusion: Matters directed by law or articles to be exercised by shareholders in general meetings
Retrospective invalidation of prior valid board acts by subsequent general meeting regulations
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from shareholder general meeting powers by vesting operational management in directors while retaining ultimate ownership authority with shareholders.

descriptors.definition: Public company boards must obtain shareholder consent via a special resolution before selling, leasing, or disposing of the whole or substantially the whole of an undertaking. This restriction does not apply to private companies or to sales conducted as part of a company's ordinary course of business.
inclusion: Selling, leasing, or disposing of whole or substantially whole undertakings
Stipulating shareholder conditions regarding sale proceeds utilization
Protecting clean title of buyers acting in good faith
exclusion: Private companies
Transactions where selling or leasing forms part of the company's ordinary business
Unauthorized capital reductions under the guise of asset sales
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general board powers under Section 179 by imposing a mandatory special resolution requirement for fundamental corporate asset disposals.

descriptors.concept_name: Charitable and Bona Fide Contributions by Company
descriptors.definition: The board of directors may contribute to bona fide charitable and other funds up to five percent of the average net profits of the three immediately preceding financial years without prior general meeting approval. Exceeding this financial limit requires prior permission from the company through an ordinary resolution in a general meeting.
inclusion: Contributions by boards up to five percent of preceding three years average net profits
Seeking ordinary resolution approval for contributions exceeding the statutory limit
Making contributions during loss years provided three-year average net profit remains positive
exclusion: Contributions exceeding five percent without prior general meeting permission
Contributions directed to non-bona fide funds
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from political and national defence contributions by its specific focus on charitable donations capped relative to average net profits.

descriptors.concept_name: Prohibitions and Restrictions Regarding Political Contributions
descriptors.definition: Eligible companies may contribute any amount directly or indirectly to registered political parties after passing an authorizing board resolution. Government companies and entities in existence for less than three financial years are strictly prohibited from making political contributions.
instrument_references: Representation of the People Act, 1951, Section 29A
inclusion: Direct or indirect contributions to registered political parties
Authorizing contributions through a meeting of the board of directors
Treating souvenir advertisements benefiting political parties as deemed contributions
Disclosing total political contributions in profit and loss accounts
exclusion: Government companies
Companies in existence for less than three financial years
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from charitable contributions under Section 181 by prohibiting certain company classes and eliminating percentage caps for political donations.

descriptors.definition: The board of directors or authorized persons may contribute unlimited amounts to the National Defence Fund or other central government-approved funds for national defence. This power has overriding effect over other statutory contribution provisions and requires profit and loss account disclosure.
inclusion: Unlimited contributions to the National Defence Fund
Contributions to funds approved by the Central Government for national defence
Disclosing total contributed amounts in the annual profit and loss account
exclusion: Restrictions imposed by Sections 180, 181, and 182 due to statutory overriding effect
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from charitable and political contributions by providing an unlimited, overriding statutory channel specifically for national defence funds.

descriptors.definition: Directors hold office in a fiduciary capacity and must make general and specific disclosures regarding any concern or interest in companies, bodies corporate, firms, or proposed contracts. General disclosure must be made at the first board meeting of participation, annually thereafter, or whenever changes occur.
instrument_references: Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules, 2014, Rule 9
inclusion: Disclosing shareholding and interest in other corporate bodies or firms
Making general disclosure at the first board meeting of participation and every financial year
Making specific disclosure when interested in contracts or arrangements
exclusion: Failing to notify changes in previously submitted disclosures at the first subsequent board meeting
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general board decision-making by placing a strict fiduciary obligation on interested directors to transparently disclose personal stakes.
